name: Chin strap for sleep

card.summary: A soft elastic band worn around the head and under the chin overnight to keep the mouth closed, used by people who want nasal breathing and a closed-mouth resting posture to support how their jaw, chin and face look.
card.note: Snoring or breathing pauses during sleep are a medical matter; a strap does not replace clinical assessment.

quick.overview:
A sleep chin strap is a stretchy band that runs under the jaw and over the top of the head so the mouth stays shut while someone sleeps. In looksmaxxing circles it is linked to mewing and nasal-breathing ideas: the aim is a closed-mouth posture through the night, which proponents associate with a better-defined jawline and less mouth breathing.

The devices come from the sleep-health world, where chin straps are used with CPAP therapy and for snoring. Published work on them concerns that clinical setting, such as whether adding a strap changes PAP use; studies of facial appearance have not been published.
quick.how: People wear a soft strap at bedtime, adjusted so the lips rest together without pulling the jaw back. Many pair it with nasal strips or nasal hygiene and with daytime tongue-posture practice (mewing). Users describe the effects as dry-mouth reduction and a habit of nasal breathing rather than visible changes in days.
quick.risks: Reported downsides include discomfort, skin marks and difficulty if the nose is blocked. Clinical sources note that mouth breathing and snoring can accompany sleep-related breathing disorders, and clinicians advise that people with suspected sleep apnea be assessed. Straps that pull the jaw backward are discussed by some users as uncomfortable.

lead: A chin strap for sleep is a band, usually elastic neoprene or fabric, that fits under the chin and over the crown to hold the lower jaw up so the mouth stays closed during sleep. It is sold for snoring and is also used with CPAP masks.

In looksmaxxing communities, it is discussed as a night-time companion to mewing: proponents say that keeping the mouth closed encourages nasal breathing, a resting tongue-to-palate posture and a firmer-looking jaw and chin line, and that it reduces the slack-jawed look associated with chronic mouth breathing. These are community beliefs rather than findings of controlled appearance studies.

Medical literature on chin straps concerns sleep-disordered breathing, for example a 2014 study on whether adding a chin strap affects PAP compliance and nightly use [1] and a 2018 case report of a patient whose sleep apnea persisted with a hypoglossal nerve stimulator until a chin strap was added [2].

angle.text: People use a soft chin strap overnight so the mouth stays closed, aiming for nasal breathing and a jaw-forward resting posture that mewing proponents associate with a cleaner jawline. The strap itself is a clinical-style accessory; the appearance benefit is a community claim.

paras: Sleep chin straps are typically one-piece bands with a cup that sits under the chin and straps meeting at the top or back of the head, with hook-and-loop adjustment. Variations include full-head caps, narrow straps and straps integrated into CPAP gear.

sections.h: How it is used and why
paras: Snoring and mouth breathing frequently occur together, and mouth breathing is described as a feature of several sleep-related breathing disorders [3]. A chin strap aims to keep the mouth closed so breathing runs through the nose.

In looksmaxxing forums, users pair the strap with mewing and nasal-breathing routines, citing a jaw that rests closed and the possible prevention of a recessed or slack lower-face look. Users report mainly practical outcomes such as less morning dry mouth.

Published work is on sleep medicine, not on appearance. A 2014 study examined the effect of adding a chin strap on PAP compliance, nightly duration of use and other factors [1]. A 2018 case report described hypoglossal-nerve-stimulator-resistant obstructive sleep apnea that resolved with the addition of a chin strap [2]. A 2023 review of managing side effects of home PAP therapy included chin straps among the interventions considered [4]. A 2012 study looked at CPAP interface and mandibular advancement device effects on upper-airway mechanics, including traction of an oronasal mask [5]. No study found tested effects on jaw shape or facial appearance.

Wikipedia notes that snoring-related mouth breathing is a feature of primary snoring, upper airway resistance syndrome and obstructive sleep apnea, and that CPAP is considered the standard treatment for sleep apnea [3]. People who snore heavily or experience breathing pauses are therefore generally directed to clinical assessment rather than self-treatment. Users also mention discomfort and difficulty if their nose is blocked.

lore.intro: Chin straps appear in discussions of mewing, nasal breathing and jaw posture as a sleep-time aid.

claims.claim: Keeping the mouth closed overnight supports a better jawline
claims.believers: Proponents of mewing say that a closed mouth and tongue-to-palate rest posture across the whole day, including sleep, matters for jaw and midface appearance.
claims.experts: No published study has tested whether a sleep chin strap changes jaw or facial appearance; the clinical studies concern PAP use and apnea [1][2].

claims.believers: Users say the strap makes mouth breathing less likely and reduces dry mouth.
claims.experts: Clinical sources describe mouth breathing as accompanying snoring and sleep-related breathing disorders [3]; a 2014 study examined chin-strap use with PAP therapy [1].
